q: ____ is the field of chemistry that is concerned with the relative quantities of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
e: Reaction stoichiometry is the field of chemistry that is concerned with the relative quantities of reactants and products in chemical reactions. Stoichiometry is the quantitative bookkeeping of how much of each substance takes part in a reaction.

q: ____ are used to describe chemical reactions; the amount of reactants used up must be equal to the amount of products formed.
e: Balanced chemical equations are used to describe chemical reactions. The amount of reactants used up must be equal to the amount of products formed. A balanced equation is the mole map of the reaction.

q: There are three laws of matter concerning chemical reactions: the ____, the Law of Definite Proportions and the Law of Multiple Proportions.
e: There are three laws of matter concerning chemical reactions: the Law of Conservation of Mass, the Law of Definite Proportions and the Law of Multiple Proportions. Mass is conserved in a chemical change: the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.

q: In all reactions, they follow the Law of Conservation of Mass. That is, the ____ of each element in reactants and products must be equal.
e: In all reactions, they follow the Law of Conservation of Mass. That is, the total number of atoms of each element in reactants and products must be equal.

q: The ____ is a substance that stoichiometrically limits the amount of product(s) that can be formed in a reaction.
e: The limiting reactant is a substance that stoichiometrically limits the amount of product(s) that can be formed in a reaction. The limiting reactant is the one that is used up first and therefore caps how much product can form.

q: The reaction will stop when all amount of the ____ is used up.
e: The reaction will stop when all amount of the limiting reactant is used up. The limiting reactant is the one that is used up first and therefore caps how much product can form.

q: The ____ = (experimental or actual yield of product / theoretical yield of product) $\times 100\%$
e: The percentage yield = (experimental or actual yield of product / theoretical yield of product) x 100%. Or actual yield of product / theoretical yield.

q: The ____ = (mass of pure substance present / mass of sample) $\times 100\%$
e: The percentage purity = (mass of pure substance present / mass of sample) x 100%. Pure substance present / mass of sample x.

q: ____ consist of linked reactions in which the product of the first reaction becomes the reactant of the second reaction.
e: Sequential reactions consist of linked reactions in which the product of the first reaction becomes the reactant of the second reaction. In sequential reactions the product of one step becomes the reactant of the next.

q: Law of Conservation of Mass states that the total mass of reactant(s) is equal to the ____ of the product(s).
e: Law of Conservation of Mass states that the total mass of reactant(s) is equal to the total mass of the product(s). Mass is conserved in a chemical change: the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.

q: Law of Multiple Proportions states that when two elements combine with each other to form more than one compound, the different masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a ratio of ____.
e: Law of Multiple Proportions states that when two elements combine with each other to form more than one compound, the different masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a ratio of small whole numbers. That comparison is with one compound, the different masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in a ratio of small whole numbers.

q: Limiting reactant is the reactant in a chemical reaction that limits the amount of product because the reaction stops when the limiting reactant is ____.
e: Limiting reactant is the reactant in a chemical reaction that limits the amount of product because the reaction stops when the limiting reactant is completely consumed. The limiting reactant is the one that is used up first and therefore caps how much product can form.
